_comment: The hooks are what make this kit work when nobody runs anything. A command an agent must choose to invoke is a suggestion; a hook that fires on its own is a mechanism. Each one calls the vendored bin/hx.cjs — no global install, no node_modules. Every hook is written so its own failure can never take down the session: hx reports the problem on stdout and exits 0 rather than blocking. Hook commands use a plain relative path (.claude/bin/hx.cjs), not $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR — that expansion is POSIX-shell syntax and silently resolves to nothing under plain PowerShell (Claude Code's Windows fallback when Git Bash is absent), which would make every hook fail to start with no error surfaced anywhere. Claude Code runs hook commands with the project root as cwd, so the relative form works identically in bash and PowerShell.

PreToolUse._comment: Denies edits to harness/secret-shaped files and a short list of destructive shell commands BEFORE the tool runs, not after. Fails closed on its own internal error (see src/kit/hooks.ts's runPreToolHook) — the one hook in this kit that does, since a protective check that silently stops protecting on its own bug is worse than useless. Escape hatches: HX_ALLOW_PROTECTED=1 / HX_ALLOW_DANGEROUS=1, or add paths to allowEdit in .claude/hx.config.json.

PostToolUse._comment: Post-hoc backstop for Bash/PowerShell (A1.8): a content-hash diff against the protected-glob snapshot SessionStart recorded, so a shell command that changes a protected/secret file is still caught even when the PreToolUse text check cannot see through it (variable expansion, a script file, an interpreter one-liner). Separate from post-edit's matcher since a shell call should only pay for a hash diff, not the full rule scan.

SessionEnd._comment: Regenerates .claude/state/progress.md and handoff.md from the feature list, git state and the event log. Before this hook existed, those files were written only if a human remembered `hx handoff` — so the two artifacts whose entire purpose is surviving the end of a session were written least reliably at the moment they mattered most.

PreCompact._comment: Compaction is the other moment session knowledge evaporates. Refreshing the handoff first means the post-compaction session can read back a current, mechanically-derived summary instead of relying on whatever survived the squeeze.

permissions._comment: allow: read-only harness commands, so routine state checks never prompt — both Bash and PowerShell forms, since PowerShell is Claude Code's default tool on Windows without Git Bash (a project running only the Bash forms would prompt on every one of these commands on such a machine). deny: the four commands that represent a human decision (issue close/wontfix, feature reopen/reset). `issue close` is also blocked inside the binary itself (it refuses --human when it detects an agent session) — this list is defence in depth, and deliberately over-matches, since a deny that is too broad costs a prompt while one that is too narrow costs the gate.
